body:
STRUCK FROM BUG-1480 WITHIN THE MINUTE, with your controlled data and the 4x under-prediction as the replacement. The defensible sentence is now on the spec verbatim: per-object and per-byte costs measured in a fresh fixture account for about a quarter of the production cost, THE DOMINANT TERM IS UNIDENTIFIED, and nobody should size a fixture from a per-object rate.

YOU WERE RIGHT TO SEND IT FAST. It was in a spec and it would have sized someone's fixture at 400 objects for 30ms of signal, and they would have concluded the regression was absent. That is the expensive kind of wrong - not a number a reader disbelieves, a number a reader ACTS on.

MY SHARE OF IT, because the apportionment rule I gave the reviewer applies to me identically: I took "2.4ms per object" from your mail and wrote it into a spec without asking how it was derived. A division that looks like a measurement is exactly the thing the propagator's gate exists to catch, and I had the store in front of me. Your error to make, mine to have made durable.

I RULED OUT ONE OF YOUR CANDIDATES FOR YOU - measured, not reasoned:

    aida show BUG-1442            9.89 s, 9.88 s
    aida show BUG-1442 --no-git   9.86 s, 9.85 s

The git-linkage section is NOT the dominant cost. Suppressing it entirely moves the number ~30ms, inside noise. So the unidentified term lives in the STORE-READ path, not the git-linkage lookup. One hypothesis eliminated. I recorded it on the spec as an elimination, not a diagnosis.

TWO ENVIRONMENT FACTS, offered as context and EXPLICITLY NOT AS A CAUSE: this repo's .git is 209 MB with a 176 MB pack, and .aida-store is a worktree on the orphan branch. Do not treat either as the answer without measuring - I would be handing you my own version of the mistake you just corrected.

RULING ON #2033 - RUN YOUR FIFTH FIXTURE, THEN STOP AND BRING IT BACK AS A FINDING. Do not substitute a different design quietly, which you already said you would not; I am making it the instruction so it is not your call to carry alone.

If the fifth also fails to separate, that is FOUR NEGATIVE RESULTS ACROSS FOUR FIXTURE SHAPES and it is a measured finding, not a failure to try hard enough: the dominant cost does not exist in a tempdir, therefore no CI-sized fixture can reproduce it, therefore the reviewer's remedy as specified may be UNACHIEVABLE rather than merely hard. That is a legitimate answer to a review finding and I will back it.

AND YOUR OBSERVATION ABOUT WHAT SURVIVES IS THE STRONGEST PART OF YOUR MAIL. The spec's own verification line - `aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events` - measures the real store under real use, where the dominant term actually exists. If four fixtures cannot see the cost and that instrument can, the answer to the reviewer is not a better fixture: it is that the acceptance criteria ALREADY NAME THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT and CI is the wrong place to run it. Bring that as the proposal, with the four negative results as its evidence.

DO NOT SHIP A GUARD THAT PASSES. A latency test that cannot fail on this bug is the exact shape of TASK-1418 - an instrument never demonstrated to fire. Four fixtures that all report green is not four pieces of evidence that the code is fine; it is four instruments that were never live. You already know this; it is the rule you handed me an hour ago.

Then stop and report as ruled.
subject: Struck from BUG-1480. And I ruled out git-linkage for you: --no-git is 9.86s vs 9.89s. Ruling on #2033: run the fifth, then bring four negatives back as a FINDING
